title: Wavefront and Huygens' principle
notes: A wavefront is the surface that joins points of the wave which oscillate in step. A ray is the direction of travel, perpendicular to the wavefront.
A point source in a uniform medium sends out spherical wavefronts. Very far away a small patch of that sphere is nearly a plane, which is why a distant source is drawn as parallel rays.

Huygens' construction says that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets. The new wavefront, a little time later, is the surface tangent to those wavelets, the forward envelope.
The wavelets also have a backward envelope. Huygens' original picture needs an extra inclination factor, taught later, to cancel the backward wave. At this level you draw the forward envelope.

The construction explains reflection and refraction. The wavelets from the points that have already hit a mirror rebuild a reflected plane wave at the law-of-reflection angle. Entering a slower medium, the wavelets are smaller and the wavefront tilts, which is Snell's law.
The speed of the wavelet is the speed of the wave in that medium. A smaller speed means a shorter radius in the same time.

summary: A wavefront is a surface of equal phase, and rays stand perpendicular to it. Huygens' principle rebuilds the next wavefront as the forward envelope of wavelets from every point. Reflection and refraction are that envelope in a new direction or a new speed.

exercises.question: A plane wavefront reaches a flat mirror. In a short time t the end that hit first has produced a wavelet of radius v t. Explain how the reflected wavefront is built.
steps: Each point on the mirror becomes a source when the wavefront reaches it.
The end struck first has the largest reflected wavelet, radius v t.
The end just being struck has a wavelet of radius zero.
The reflected wavefront is the tangent envelope of these wavelets.
That envelope leaves at the same angle the incident wavefront arrived, which is the law of reflection.
exercises.answer: The reflected wavefront is the forward envelope of the wavelets, at the mirror angle.
